Your agent drafts it. You finish it by hand.

AI agents already write a landing page in seconds. Changing it still means digging through code. In Kalka, what your agent writes lands on the canvas as real layers: move them, restyle them, keep what works.

  3. 3

Nothing to relearn. Nothing to rebuild.

Every layer is an element

The layers panel is the DOM. Select a layer, its tag is right there. Edit the code, the canvas follows.

Layers Desktop header section.hero h1 p a.btn section.mosaic
section.hero
<body>
<header>…</header>
<section class="hero">
<h1>…</h1>
<p>…</p>
<a class="btn">…</a>
</section>
<section class="mosaic">…

If you know Figma, you know Kalka

Same panels, same tools, same habits. Open it and start designing.

shader layer

Shaders, live on the canvas

Mesh gradients, grain, flowing light. Tune them like any other layer.

Made for everyone between the mockup and the launch.

Designers

What you draw is what ships. No more "it looked different in the mockup". Your shadows, your spacing, your type, exactly.

Developers

Get real HTML and CSS, not a picture to reverse engineer. Diff it, review it, merge it like the rest of your code.

Agencies and freelancers

Cut the rebuild out of every project. Deliver sooner, with fewer rounds of "can you move this 4px".

The words you design with, the properties the web runs on.

Kalka keeps the vocabulary designers love and writes the CSS developers expect. Figma to HTML, without a plugin or an export step.

Your work stays yours.

Plain files HTML, CSS and JSON in a folder you own. Open it in any code editor.
Git, built in Branch, diff and review a design the same way you review code.
On your machine A desktop app. Your projects never have to leave your computer.
Free, for real The app and the local MCP server are MIT licensed. No seat to pay for, no usage cap.
Explorer
      • home.html
      • pricing.html
    • styles.css
      • tokens.json
    • project.json

Built in the open. Free where it counts.

Kalka is built around the browser itself. The desktop app and the local MCP server stay free and MIT licensed. A hosted version for teams will come later, as an optional subscription.

Follow the build on X, @bedleybuilds

Questions, answered.

Is Kalka free?

Yes. The desktop app and the local MCP server are free and open source under the MIT license. A hosted version for teams will come later, as an option.
